The fixture for a mark no page prints in a Typst index (M117, M118).
Quarto's Typst template does not print `description:`, so the label of each
mark written there names no element. An entry whose marks are all such
marks, with no cross-reference that prints and no sub-entry that prints, is
left out of the index, and so is a letter group none of whose entries
prints. A cross-reference prints where a mark that writes it is on a page
and its target prints.

The description writes seventeen marks. `Halyard` and `Hawser` are marked
there alone, and are the only terms of their letter, so the index prints
neither them nor an `H` heading. `Bitt` is also marked in the body, on page
2, so it prints that page alone. `Cleat!Horn` is a sub-entry under a parent
marked in the body, so `Cleat` prints and `Horn` does not. `Davit`,
`Fender`, `Fender!Rope` and `Gaff` print with no page number, each above a
sub-entry that prints. `Rig` opens a range there that closes on page 2, so
its closing mark is on a page: `Rig` prints, with no page number.
`Mast!Step` does the same as a sub-entry, so `Mast`, which has no mark of
its own, prints above it.

Four of the description's marks write a cross-reference. `Oar, see Paddle`
and `Winch, see also Bitt` are written there alone, so neither prints, and
nor does an `O` or a `W` heading. `Boom` is marked there alone, above
`Boom!Vang`, whose only mark there writes `see Bitt`, so neither prints.
`Thwart, see Paddle` is also written in the body, so it prints.

`Sheave` is left out, so a cross-reference to it does not print: `Block`
has no other content and is left out, `Jib`, whose only cross-reference is
to `Block`, is left out too, and `Clew` prints its second target alone.
`Tack` and `Yawl` point at each other from the body, and both print.
`Keel` points at `Rudder`, which no mark files, and keeps it, with the one
report this render writes.

`Thole` is marked in the second index there alone, and the body's one mark
in that index writes `Pin, see Thole`, so the second index prints nothing:
no heading, no line in the table of contents and no page.

The body marks a parent that prints its page: [Cleat]{.index}, and the
target of a cross-reference: [Paddle]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

The body marks a term the description marks too: [Bitt]{.index}.

A sub-entry prints under a parent the description alone marks:
[arm]{.index entry="Davit!Arm"}.

A sub-entry two levels down prints under two such entries:
[eye]{.index entry="Fender!Rope!Eye"}.

A sub-entry with a cross-reference and no page prints under such a parent:
[jaw]{.index entry="Gaff!Jaw" see="Bitt"}.

A term with a cross-reference and no page prints:
[kedge]{.index entry="Kedge" see="Bitt"}.

A cross-reference the description also writes prints:
[thwart]{.index entry="Thwart" see="Paddle"}.

A cross-reference to a term the index leaves out does not print:
[block]{.index entry="Block" see="Sheave"}.

A cross-reference to a term left out for that reason does not print:
[jib]{.index entry="Jib" see="Block"}.

Of two targets, the one the index leaves out does not print:
[clew]{.index entry="Clew" see="Sheave"} and
[clew]{.index entry="Clew" see="Paddle"}.

Two terms point at each other: [tack]{.index entry="Tack" see="Yawl"} and
[yawl]{.index entry="Yawl" see="Tack"}.

A target no mark files: [keel]{.index entry="Keel" see="Rudder"}.

A cross-reference in the second index to a term left out there:
[thole pin]{.index index="spare" entry="Pin" see="Thole"}.

The range the description opens closes here: [Rig]{.index range="close"},
and so does a sub-entry's: [step]{.index entry="Mast!Step" range="close"}.
